name: Brass Knuckles
oracle_text:
When you cast this spell, copy it. (The copy becomes a token.)
Equipped creature has double strike as long as two or more Equipment are attached to it.
Equip {1} ({1}: Attach to target creature you control. Equip only as a sorcery.)
blocked_sentences: Equipped creature has double strike as long as two or more Equipment are attached to it.

needs.what: a way for a filter to name the permanents attached to a given host -- the Equipment and Auras hanging off the creature this Equipment is itself attached to -- so a static's `condition` can be `{"cmp": ">=", "left": {"count": {"subtypes": ["Equipment"], "attached_to_host": true}}, "right": {"const": 2}}`. Concretely: a `static_filter_keys` entry (and its twin in `selector_keys`) that matches every battlefield object whose `attached_to` equals the SOURCE's `attached_to`, i.e. its fellow attachments, including the source itself so "two or more" counts the printed way. It is board state (`GameObject.attached_to`) like the existing `attached` key, so it is a pipeline input and safe inside a static.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `attached` is the only attachment word a static filter has and it points the OTHER way: `characteristics._matches` short-circuits `if selector.get("attached"): return obj.oid == source.attached_to`, so it matches exactly one object -- the host this Equipment is stapled to -- which is how "equipped creature has double strike" is written. Combined with `subtypes: ["Equipment"]` it matches the equipped CREATURE and therefore counts 0, never the other Equipment on it. `effects/selectors.py` spells `attached` the same way (`oid not in (source.attached_to, source.last_attached_to)`), so the wider selector language cannot say it either. `is_attached` (in `static_condition_keys`) is a yes/no about the source's own `attached_to`/`attached_to_player` and carries no filter and no count, so it cannot ask how many Equipment share a host; `counters` counts counters, not permanents; and `count`/`exists` in `static_value_keys`/`static_condition_keys` can only be handed a filter built from `static_filter_keys`, which has no key relating one attachment to another. Writing the static with no condition, or with a condition that is merely "this Equipment is attached", would grant double strike off a single Equipment -- a strictly stronger card.
